editorial.headline: Growth-Regulator Manufacturing With a Bali Stop Sign
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 20213 covers chemical processing into growth regulators, nationally foreign-open but currently blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 20213 is a manufacturing activity, not a trading label or a broad agricultural catch-all. The slim record defines it as the processing of chemical materials into growth-regulating substances: atonik, ethrel, cepha, dekamon, mixtalol, hidrasil, and sitozim are the examples named in the scope. In plain English, this is the industrial making of chemical products used to regulate plant growth. The emphasis is on the processing activity itself, and the record gives no further permissions, technical thresholds, product registrations, or operational conditions beyond that scope.

The registration profile is unusually broad on business scale. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales, so the category is not framed only for large factories. A small operator and a large operator sit inside the same activity description if the activity is genuinely the processing of chemical materials into these growth-regulating substances. That scale openness matters because it tells a founder where the KBLI can sit structurally in OSS-style business classification terms; it does not, by itself, create any additional licence, timeline, facility standard, or capital requirement not written in the record.

Nationally, the PMA picture is clear. The record marks the activity as TERBUKA and gives pma_max_asing as 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Rendered as a founder would read it, the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. On the national classification alone, therefore, this is a foreign-open activity. There is no partial foreign cap in the record, no stated Indonesian partner requirement, and no separate national caveat beyond the fields supplied here.

Bali changes the practical answer. The record sets l4_bali_blocked to true and marks the Bali status as BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. The reason is explicit: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope → blocked by Bali moratorium 13 May 2026.” The moratorium rule in the record says Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent, with the source identified as Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. That means the honest Bali lede is not that the activity is nationally open, although it is; it is that a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today under the record provided.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally this is a foreign-open manufacturing activity, but the Bali record turns the practical PMA answer into a block.
